title: Khayr al-Dīn Khayyām, the Andalusī mercenary captain who led the crusaders' army in Tuscany, dies in camp
A daughter, Lubnā, is born to the heir Ismāʿīl

The empire is given a Shaykh al-Islām, the authority over all the muftīs: he writes fatwās, appoints the regional muftīs and guards the legality of the Emperor's edicts. He is to be a Mālikī. Offered the most loyal muftī, the most learned, or a famous Ṣūfī, the Emperor chooses the Ṣūfī

data.text: Where the Qāḍī are the judges of the land, the Muftī are the ones to provide general legal interpretation and doctrine. A Monarchy as large as ours, however, needs an overarching authority over all Muftī. Traditionally this is the role of the Šayḵ al-Islām. The Šayḵ al-Islām will not only author Fatwā himself, he will also be the one to appoint many of the regional Muftī in our realm, and ultimately he is the person who will safeguard the legality of the Emperor's edicts. Naturally the man we pick will belong to the Mālikī but there are a number of distinguished candidates to choose from (the game's text)
options: Let us elect the foremost and most loyal Muftī to this position
The most learned and steadfast candidate must be named Šayḵ al-Islām
A famous Sufi will give this office the dignity it deserves: mysticism +10 (then 34.04); the Emperor gains a Sufi Šayḵ al-Islām until death, +0.10 monthly legitimacy
data.chosen: A famous Ṣūfī: the save of 10 October 1435 shows the Emperor's sufi_modifier from 27 September 1434
